dataset_source.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
dataset_source.attribution: Source data: Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna and Miguel A. L. Marques, Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds, Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:qv-bq, CC BY 4.0. This catalogue is a derived projection with additional source-state screening commentary.

scope: Previously private source-model screening is now published as unscored source-computed material-design hypotheses. Historical private-screening wording is retained as context. These predictions are new to this reviewed catalogue only; experimental confirmation, worldwide first discovery, formal RPS and human scientific review are not claimed.
source_tc_scope: Source isotropic Eliashberg Tc in K at mu*=0.1 is a model result, not experimental Tc. It is a separate source product and is not associated with an individual Gaussian width or a numerical uncertainty interval.
pairing_response_scope: Retained ten-width lambda contrasts and independent source Tc products support bounded source-model comparisons. Chemical, mass, volume, sampling, spin and SOC effects can co-change; no universal causal or error-bound interpretation is assigned.
risk_tag_scope: Attention labels support browsing. Element labels are not measured magnetic ground states, rejection criteria or calibrated potential scores; no label does not mean no risk.

candidate.prototype: Pm-3m five-site ordered hydrogen intermetallic cage: H 1a, Hf 1b, Ru three edge-center sites
candidate.prototype_evidence: Pm-3m five-site ordered hydrogen intermetallic cage: H 1a, Hf 1b, Ru three edge-center sites
candidate.support_meaning: Preliminary screened support within the stated source model. This ordinal level is not a probability, formal RPS score or human scientific review.
candidate.risk_summary: Hydrogen zero-point/anharmonic and vacancy/decomposition energetics, ordering entropy and Hf/Ru SOC may alter the prediction. The actual target has no signed negative finite-path value and positive Gamma optical compression. Ti3HfH is better at all ten lambda values and remains a retained negative control for the claim of globally optimal chemistry; it does not contradict the narrower Hf-for-V hypothesis.
candidate.ambient_scope: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=-0.056 GPa, full max stress=0.056 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
candidate.route_response: Hf replaces V on the unique cage-corner cation site with the three Ru and one H roles retained. Cell volume rises 10.763%, H-Ru distance rises 0.0660796 A and Hf-Ru versus V-Ru rises 0.0934507 A. This coupled cation/network construction increases source lambda across all ten sigma values; it is not an expansion-only causal attribution.
candidate.next_action: Compare HfRu3H and VRu3H at a common cage volume, identical PP/cutoff and q/k sampling, and include H vacancy/decomposition or anharmonic stability evidence. Persistence of the lambda gain supports the coupled construction; collapse of the gain or a nontranslation soft branch opposes it.

seven_criteria.identity: Complete ordered CIF/literal coarse-fine input/Gamma periodic species-site association is numerically supported; source input geometry and full tensor/forces are retained. Export occupancy is a discrete computational convention; source experimental P/T/occupancy and actual compiled unit constant are unknown. Exact-version input defaults scope the configured neutral scalar spin1/noSOC model, not magnetic ground state.
seven_criteria.quantitative_route_response: Hf replaces V on the unique cage-corner cation site with the three Ru and one H roles retained. Cell volume rises 10.763%, H-Ru distance rises 0.0660796 A and Hf-Ru versus V-Ru rises 0.0934507 A. This coupled cation/network construction increases source lambda across all ten sigma values; it is not an expansion-only causal attribution.
seven_criteria.pairing_relevance: Exact target and mapped control direct source lambda arrays have the same favorable sign at all ten common broadening tokens; omega_ln has explicit K units and separate Eli/McM mu=.1 tables remain independent. Same underlying q mesh is observed. The sensitivity range is not a physical error bound; sigma units, full-BZ convergence, experimental Tc and pure-geometry causality remain unknown. Literal method differences are declared confounds.
seven_criteria.ambient_feasibility: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=-0.056 GPa, full max stress=0.056 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
seven_criteria.competition_and_coherence: Hydrogen zero-point/anharmonic and vacancy/decomposition energetics, ordering entropy and Hf/Ru SOC may alter the prediction. The actual target has no signed negative finite-path value and positive Gamma optical compression. Ti3HfH is better at all ten lambda values and remains a retained negative control for the claim of globally optimal chemistry; it does not contradict the narrower Hf-for-V hypothesis.
seven_criteria.novelty: Exact HfRu3H/HRu3Hf superconductivity queries on 2026-10-07 identified no experimental superconducting exact ordered phase. The MC2023 published prediction is acknowledged prior, and only the matched Hf-for-V source hypothesis is proposed as new to this reviewed catalogue.
seven_criteria.decision: Compare HfRu3H and VRu3H at a common cage volume, identical PP/cutoff and q/k sampling, and include H vacancy/decomposition or anharmonic stability evidence. Persistence of the lambda gain supports the coupled construction; collapse of the gain or a nontranslation soft branch opposes it.
